protocol_type: Command/response time-division multiplex serial bus. The Bus Controller (BC) issues a Command Word (BC → RT); the addressed Remote Terminal (RT) responds with a Status Word (RT → BC) and optionally Data Words.

opcodes.description: Mode Code: requests handoff of bus control to the addressed RT (target acknowledges by setting Dynamic Bus Acceptance bit).
Mode Code: forces the addressed RT to synchronize to the BC (no data word).
Mode Code: re-issue last Status Word (Mode Code 00010, mandatory).
Mode Code: command the RT to initiate its built-in self test (BIT).
Mode Code: shut down the redundant bus transmitter on the addressed RT (used for fault containment).
Mode Code: re-enable the previously-shut-down transmitter.
Mode Code: mask the Terminal Flag bit in the Status Word.
Mode Code: un-mask the Terminal Flag bit in the Status Word.
Mode Code: force the addressed RT to reset its state.
Mode Code with Data: RT sends a 16-bit Vector Word (acyclic service-request data).
Mode Code with Data: BC sends a data word for synchronization use.
Mode Code with Data: RT echoes the last Command Word it received (mandatory).
Mode Code with Data: RT sends its Built-In-Test (BIT) word (mandatory).
Mode Code with Data: shut down a specifically-selected transmitter (data word identifies which).
Mode Code with Data: re-enable specifically-selected transmitter.

channels.name: Bus A (primary)
channels.description: Primary 78 Ω twinax bus carrying Manchester II 1 Mbit/s; selected by BC for each message; transformer-coupled stubs.

channels.name: Bus B (redundant)
channels.description: Standby 78 Ω twinax bus identical to Bus A; selected by BC for retry or failover; messages travel on only one of A/B at a time.

frame_types.name: Command Word
frame_types.purpose: BC → RT control word: addresses an RT, selects T/R, names a Subaddress / Mode Code, and gives Word Count or Mode Code value.

frame_types.name: Status Word
frame_types.purpose: RT → BC response word: echoes RT address and reports up to 9 status bits (Message Error, Service Request, Busy, Terminal Flag, etc.).

frame_types.name: Data Word
frame_types.purpose: 16-bit payload word; 0..32 per message; carries subsystem application data or mode-command data.

data_frame_fields.value: Command/Status: HIGH 1.5µs → LOW 1.5µs ; Data: LOW 1.5µs → HIGH 1.5µs

data_frame_fields.components: 0-30 valid; 31 = broadcast (Command Word only). Echoed in Status Word.
Command Word only. 1 = RT transmits to BC; 0 = RT receives from BC.
Command Word: 1-30 = data subaddress; 0 or 31 = Mode Code (selector). Status Word: status bits at the same offsets.
Command Word: when Subaddress ≠ 0/31 → Word Count (1-32; 0=32). When Subaddress = 0/31 → Mode Code (00000 .. 10101).
Data Word payload. 0..32 Data Words per message.

data_frame_fields.value: odd parity over the 16 data bits of the same word

rows: Maximum non-zero count; 32 is encoded as all-zero.
data_length_code_encoding.note: 5-bit Word Count field encodes 1..32 data words; binary value 00000 is interpreted as 32 (max-data shortcut).

remote_frame_rules: A Command Word with T/R = 1 ('transmit') is a 'remote' / pull request to the addressed RT.
The addressed RT responds: Status Word + N Data Words within 4-12 µs.
If the RT cannot satisfy the request, it sets MESSAGE ERROR + does not transmit data.
Broadcast (RT address 31) inhibits the Status Word response — the receiving RTs accept data silently.
valid_ready_handshake_rules: There is no AMBA-style per-cycle VALID/READY handshake.
Per-message handshake: BC sends Command (+ Data) → RT sends Status (+ Data) within 4-12 µs.
The Status Word's MESSAGE ERROR bit + BUSY bit + SERVICE REQUEST bit + BROADCAST COMMAND RECEIVED bit provide message-level back-pressure / error signalling.
BC enforces the 4 µs minimum inter-message gap before launching the next Command Word.
No-response timeout = 14 µs of bus quiet after the last command word → BC declares 'no response' and may retry on Bus B.
byte_order_within_data_field: MSB-first (bit 1 of the 16-bit data word is the most significant bit). Multi-word payload ordering is application-defined.

interframe_space.rt_response_window: 4 µs to 12 µs after the last bit of the BC's command word
interframe_space.broadcast_gap: Same 4 µs minimum; no RT status response in broadcast
